reason: Re-opened Sāyaṇa on 7.33.7 through packet.js --verse 7.33.7 and by fetching the pinned revision 327730 raw: the evidence stands verbatim. His own gloss makes the three who make seed in the worlds (earth, mid-air, sky) Agni, Vāyu and Sūrya in order, the same three the shining ones who attend the dawn, and the three noble peoples ‘headed by Āditya’; the naming of those peoples as Vasus, Rudras and Ādityas is the Śāṭyāyanaka’s, which he quotes with tathā ca in support, and the sentence marks it ‘citing the Śāṭyāyanaka’, so nothing of the quoted text is passed off as his own coinage. Wilson’s note (‘Sayana quotes Satyayana for the explanation of this verse’) confirms. Verse: verse.js ok, 7.33.7 at [548,7], whole verse, 31 words, no dash. Plain: 7.33 is on the Vasisthas, their help in the Ten Kings battle and Vasistha’s birth (vv. 10 to 13); ‘credits them with a threefold lore’ summarises the verse without a line-by-line paraphrase or a four-word run; the clause omits the battle but says nothing false. Drift: none; ‘Sun’ for Sūrya/Āditya and ‘air’ for antarikṣa are fair. The watch term ‘Aryan’ is avoided (the verse’s āryāḥ is not mentioned). entry-check.js ok, no errors or warnings.
better: Optional placement: ‘Between the Ten Kings battle and the tale of Vasistha’s birth, the verse credits the Vasisthas with a threefold lore’ would say where the verse stands, not only what the hymn is about.
